label: Bookkeeping
project: 2025 books catch-up and monthly close setup
summary: Bring 9 months of behind QuickBooks Online books current, then move to a monthly close.
billing: Flat project fee for the cleanup/catch-up (commonly $500 to $5,000+ by months behind and account count, quoted after reviewing the trial balance), then a fixed monthly fee for ongoing close. Sources: xenett.com cleanup guide, sdocpa.com monthly bookkeeping.
ms: Done means bank, card, payroll and loan feeds are connected, the trial balance is reviewed and the fixed quote is signed.
Accountant user invited to QuickBooks Online
Bank and credit card feeds connected
Prior tax return and year-end balances received
Done means every transaction January to September is categorized and the uncategorized/Ask My Accountant balance is zero.
Uncategorized transactions list sent to client
Client answers on unknown items applied
Owner draws and loans split out
Sales tax and merchant fees booked
Done means every bank, card and loan account reconciles to statements through September 30 with no unexplained differences.
Loan balance tied to lender statement
Done means a reviewed P&L and balance sheet are delivered and the first monthly close is on the calendar.
waiting: Answers on the uncategorized-transactions list (what a payment or deposit was for) and missing bank or card statements.
ask: How should owner payments be handled going forward?
Owner draws from the business account
Affects how the books and the tax return treat money taken out.
answered: Which accounting software to standardize on?
checkin: - Done: January to June categorized and reconciled
- Next: July to September categorization, card reconciliations
- Needs from you: 23 unknown transactions on the list, August and September Amex statements
talk: Hi Maria, there are 23 transactions we can't identify, mostly Venmo and Zelle. Can you mark what each was for in the list?
Most of the Venmo ones are flower market purchases, I'll go through it tonight.
Perfect. Once those are in we can reconcile through September and send you clean statements next week.
anxieties: When will my books actually be done?
Will this be ready in time for my tax preparer?
What do I do with the receipts I lost?
notes: Engagements are fairly standard (cleanup then recurring), but scope varies wildly by how far behind and how many accounts. Portal must handle bank statements and financial data securely; bookkeepers are not regulated like CPAs but handle sensitive data and often bank credentials (portal should never store login credentials). Third-party deadline: tax filing deadlines drive urgency.

label: Tax preparation (individual)
summary: Prepare and e-file a joint return with a Schedule C side business and a rental.
billing: Flat fee per return, usually set by forms and schedules (base 1040 plus per-schedule add-ons), often paid before the return is released or e-filed. Source: TaxDome tax preparation process docs (returns can be locked to invoices).
ms: Done means the engagement letter and consent are signed and the tax organizer is submitted.
ID and prior-year return on file
Done means every W-2, 1099, 1098, K-1 and expense summary on the checklist is uploaded or marked not applicable.
Schedule C income and expense summary
Done means the return is prepared, reviewed by a second preparer, and open questions are answered.
Done means Form 8879 is e-signed, the invoice is paid, and the IRS and state acceptance is received.
waiting: Missing documents, most often a late K-1, a corrected 1099, or brokerage tax statements.
ask: How should we handle the balance due?
Direct debit on a chosen date
Set up an IRS installment agreement
File an extension and pay an estimate
An extension extends time to file, not time to pay.
answered: Refund or apply to next year?
checkin: - Done: organizer and W-2s received, draft started
- Next: rental schedule and review
- Needs from you: brokerage 1099 composite, 2025 estimated payment dates
talk: Hi James, we're still missing the Fidelity 1099. It usually posts mid-February, can you upload it when it's out?
It says corrected forms might come in March, should I wait?
Upload what's there now. If a corrected one comes we'll update before filing.
anxieties: Will I get a refund or owe?
Do I need an extension?
Is my upload secure?
notes: Highly standardized seasonal workflow. Compliance: IRC 7216 consent for use/disclosure of tax info, IRS Pub 4557 data security (WISP required under FTC Safeguards Rule), 8879 signatures need identity verification (KBA). Portal must not give tax advice by itself. Third-party deadlines: April 15 / October 15, IRS acceptance and rejections.

label: Tax preparation (small business)
summary: Prepare and file the S corporation return by March 16 and issue the owner's K-1.
billing: Flat fee per entity return (often $1,500 to $5,000 depending on books quality), frequently with a surcharge if books need cleanup first; billed at engagement deposit plus balance on delivery. Source: TaxDome proposals and engagement letters, vendor pricing guides.
ms: Done means the engagement letter is signed and the year-end trial balance and bank reconciliations are received.
Bookkeeper access or year-end trial balance
Done means payroll (W-2s, 941s) ties to the books and year-end adjusting entries are approved.
Done means the 1120-S, state return and draft K-1 are reviewed and sent for client review.
Done means Form 8879-S is signed, returns are accepted, and the K-1 is in the owner's portal.
waiting: Year-end books (trial balance and reconciliations) and the fixed asset purchases list.
ask: Take Section 179 on the new truck this year?
Changes this year's tax and the owner's K-1.
checkin: - Done: trial balance received, payroll tied out
- Next: depreciation, draft return
- Needs from you: truck purchase invoice, decision on Section 179
talk: Daniel, payroll ties out. We need the truck invoice and your call on Section 179 before we draft.
Uploaded the invoice. What saves more this year?
Full expensing saves more now but less later. We'll show both numbers on tomorrow's call.
anxieties: Will we make the March deadline?
How much will I owe personally from the K-1?
Do I need to pay estimated taxes?
notes: Fairly standard per entity type but quality of client books drives scope. Same 7216, WISP and 8879 rules. Third-party deadlines: March 15 (1120-S, 1065, shifted to next business day), April 15 (1120), extension via 7004. Delivering K-1s to other owners is a confidentiality boundary (each owner sees only their own).

label: Small-business accounting / fractional CFO
project: Fractional CFO onboarding and first 90 days
summary: Assessment, 13-week cash forecast and monthly reporting package ahead of a bank line-of-credit ask.
billing: Monthly retainer (roughly $3,000 to $15,000 by complexity), often preceded by a paid assessment ($5,000 to $10,000, 2 to 3 weeks); board packs often an add-on tier. Sources: sdocpa.com fractional CFO cost, beancount.io fractional CFO guide.
ms: Done means the assessment report and 90-day roadmap are delivered and walked through.
Done means the forecast ties to AR/AP and the owner reviews it weekly.
Done means the annual budget is approved and the KPI dashboard is live.
Done means the line-of-credit package (financials, forecast, narrative) is sent to the bank.
waiting: AR/AP agings and answers about upcoming large purchases or hires that change the forecast.
ask: How big a line of credit to request?
Forecast shows the low point in March; bigger lines cost more in fees.
checkin: - Done: assessment and forecast v1
- Next: budget assumptions, KPI picks
- Needs from you: hiring plan for Q1, new roaster lease terms
talk: Alicia, the forecast shows cash dipping to about $18k in early March. Want to walk through options Thursday?
Yes. Is that before or after the wholesale invoices come in?
Before. Pulling the wholesale terms in by 15 days fixes most of it, we'll show both cases.
anxieties: Am I going to run out of cash?
Can I afford this hire?
Will the bank approve us?
notes: Very bespoke; deliverables recur monthly rather than ending. If a CPA firm, AICPA independence and confidentiality apply; not investment advice. Third-party deadlines: lender and board meetings, covenant reporting dates.

label: Estate planning law
summary: Joint revocable trust package with pour-over wills, powers of attorney, health care directives and deed.
billing: Flat fee package (consumer guides put trust packages around $1,500 to $5,000), commonly 50 percent at engagement and 50 percent at signing; deed and funding sometimes extra. Sources: piercelaw.com flat fee Q&A, thehivelaw.com pricing.
ms: Done means the intake questionnaire is complete and the plan design (trustees, guardians, beneficiaries) is agreed.
Done means the clients have reviewed drafts and all requested changes are made.
Done means all documents are signed, witnessed and notarized.
Done means the house deed is recorded to the trust and funding instructions for accounts are complete.
waiting: The completed intake questionnaire and asset list, then comments on the drafts.
ask: The person who manages the trust if both of you cannot.
answered: Who is guardian for minor children?
checkin: - Done: design meeting, drafts sent
- Next: revisions, schedule signing
- Needs from you: comments on the trust draft, witness availability
talk: Hi Robert and Linda, drafts are in your portal. Please send comments by Friday so we can hold the signing on the 14th.
One question, can our son be co-trustee with my sister?
Yes. We'll revise to co-trustees and note whether they must act together.
anxieties: Is the trust done once I sign?
Do I need to retitle my accounts?
What happens if we move states?
notes: Fairly templated packages with family-specific choices. Privileged communications; documents contain full financial picture; execution formalities (witnesses, notary) cannot be replaced by e-signature in many states. Earned-upon-receipt vs trust account handling of advance fees varies by state. Third-party deadlines: county recorder for deed.

label: Immigration law
summary: Concurrent I-130, I-485, I-765 and I-131 filing for a spouse in the US.
billing: Flat fee per case (about $2,500 to $7,000 for marriage AOS) often in installments, plus USCIS fees paid separately; RFE responses and interview prep sometimes extra. Sources: lighthousehq.com, manifestlaw.com.
ms: Done means the engagement is signed, eligibility screened and the document checklist issued.
Done means forms are prepared, reviewed by both spouses and signed, with bona fide marriage evidence assembled.
Done means USCIS receipt notices are issued and biometrics is attended.
Work permit and travel doc tracked
Done means the interview is held and the green card is approved.
waiting: Bona fide marriage evidence and the I-864 sponsor financial documents.
ask: Who will be the financial sponsor?
Income must meet 125 percent of poverty guidelines.
answered: File work permit and travel document with it?
Yes, file I-765 and I-131 concurrently
checkin: - Done: forms drafted, most evidence received
- Next: medical exam, final signing
- Needs from you: 2024 tax transcript, more joint evidence
talk: Elena, we have the photos and lease. Could you add any joint bank or insurance statements?
We only opened a joint account last month, is that okay?
Yes, send it. Recent is fine, we'll pair it with the lease and insurance.
anxieties: How long will USCIS take?
Can I travel or work while it's pending?
What if we get an RFE?
notes: Moderately standard by petition type but timelines are owned entirely by USCIS and consulates and swing by months. Privileged, highly sensitive identity documents (passports, A-numbers); clients may need multilingual support. Fees and forms change (USCIS fee rule); portal must not promise processing times.

label: Family law / divorce
summary: Divorce with a shared custody plan and division of the house and retirement accounts.
billing: Hourly against an advance retainer (often $3,000 to $10,000+) held in the client trust account (IOLTA) and replenished when low; invoices show draws. Sources: LeanLaw trust accounting for family law, Minnesota LPRB IOLTA guidance.
ms: Done means the petition and summons are filed and proof of service is on file.
Done means both sides have served full declarations of disclosure with schedules of assets and debts.
Done means a signed marital settlement agreement and parenting plan exist, or trial issues are narrowed.
Done means the judgment is signed by the court and entered, after the waiting period.
waiting: Financial disclosure documents (statements, pay stubs, tax returns) and retainer replenishment.
ask: Goes into the parenting plan proposal.
answered: Keep the house or sell it?
checkin: - Done: petition served, our disclosures drafted
- Next: serve disclosures, schedule mediation
- Needs from you: 401k statement, retainer top-up
talk: Sarah, we need your latest 401k statement to finish the asset schedule. Also, your retainer is below the minimum.
I'll download the statement tonight. How much do I need to add?
The agreement says back to $5,000, so $2,150. The invoice is in your portal.
anxieties: How long until this is final?
How much is this going to cost?
What does my ex see?
notes: Highly variable by conflict level. Trust accounting rules (no commingling, earned fees only, refunds of unused retainer). Privilege and safety: opposing spouse may share devices or emails, so portal access and notifications must be discreet. Court-owned deadlines and statutory waiting periods (e.g. California six months from service).

label: Small-business legal
person: Tom Alvarez and Nina Brooks (Fieldstone Studio)
project: LLC formation and client contract templates
summary: Form a two-member LLC with an operating agreement, then draft a master services agreement.
billing: Flat fee per package (attorney formation packages about $550 to $1,500 plus state fees; operating agreements $750 to $3,500; contract drafting $500 to $2,500), some firms on a monthly subscription. Sources: surge.law pricing, Local First Arizona fee schedule.
ms: Done means articles of organization are accepted by the state and the EIN is issued.
Done means both members have e-signed the operating agreement.
Done means initial state reports, BOI or local licenses and a compliance calendar are in place.
Done means the master services agreement and SOW template are final.
waiting: Decisions on ownership split, capital contributions and buyout terms.
checkin: - Done: LLC filed, EIN issued
- Next: operating agreement draft
- Needs from you: capital amounts, what happens if one of you leaves
talk: Tom and Nina, the LLC is approved. Before we draft, what happens to a member's share if they leave in year one?
We were thinking the other person can buy it at what they put in.
That works. We'll draft a buyout at capital contributed for the first two years.
anxieties: Is my personal liability protected now?
What filings do I owe each year?
Can I sign client contracts yet?
notes: Packaged and repeatable for formation, variable for contracts. Privilege; e-signature fine for most business docs. State filing offices own processing times. Flat fees paid in advance may need trust account handling depending on state.

label: Real estate agent (buyer side)
summary: Accepted offer on a single-family home, 30-day financed close.
billing: Commission paid at closing (no per-stage billing). Since August 17, 2024, a signed written buyer agreement stating compensation is required before touring; seller may still offer to pay. Source: NAR settlement resource for homebuyers.
ms: Done means the contract is fully signed and earnest money is delivered to escrow.
Done means inspections are done and repairs or credits are agreed, or the contingency is removed.
Done means the appraisal meets the price and the lender issues clear to close.
Done means the final walkthrough is done, documents signed, deed recorded and keys handed over.
waiting: Documents and responses for the lender and signing contingency removals on time.
ask: What to ask for after the inspection?
Roof is near end of life; credit is cleanest.
checkin: - Done: earnest money in, inspection done
- Next: repair request, appraisal
- Needs from you: decision on repair ask by Wednesday
talk: Inspection report is in your folder. The big item is the roof. I'd ask for an $8,000 credit.
Will they say no and walk?
Unlikely, the report backs it. Contingency ends Thursday so let's send it today.
anxieties: Are we still on track to close on time?
Did the appraisal come in?
Is it safe to wire money (wire fraud)?
notes: Milestones are standard but dates come from the contract and vary by state. Third parties own most deadlines (lender, appraiser, title, escrow). Wire fraud is the biggest risk: portal must never send wiring instructions by plain message. Agents cannot give legal advice; state license rules on disclosures and record retention.

label: Real estate agent (seller side)
summary: Prepare, list and close the sale of a three-bedroom townhome.
billing: Commission percentage paid from sale proceeds at closing under the listing agreement; seller may separately agree to pay buyer-agent compensation, which cannot be advertised on the MLS. Source: NAR settlement resources.
ms: Done means the listing agreement and disclosures are signed and the home is staged and photographed.
Done means the listing is live, showings and open houses are running and feedback is shared.
Done means an offer is accepted and the buyer's inspection and appraisal contingencies are resolved.
Done means the seller signs, the deed records and proceeds are wired.
waiting: Seller disclosure forms and access for photos, showings and repairs.
ask: Cash closes in 14 days with no appraisal.
checkin: - Done: photos, disclosures signed
- Next: go live Thursday, open house Saturday
- Needs from you: HOA documents and a spare key
talk: Gloria, we go live Thursday. Can you leave the HOA docs and a spare key by Wednesday?
Yes. Should I be home during the open house?
Better not. I'll text you feedback right after.
anxieties: Why haven't we had offers?
Should we drop the price?
How much will I net?
notes: Standard phases, variable time on market. State disclosure laws, brokerage compliance review of files, seller-paid compensation rules post-NAR settlement. Title, escrow and buyer's lender own closing dates.

label: Mortgage broker
project: 30-year fixed purchase loan for 418 Maple Ave
summary: Purchase loan from application to funding on a 30-day close.
billing: Compensated per loan, either lender-paid or borrower-paid compensation (a percentage of the loan amount) at closing; not billed per stage. Regulated by loan originator compensation rules. Source: Guaranteed Rate loan processing guide, Bankrate conditional approval.
ms: Done means the application is submitted, the Loan Estimate issued and intent to proceed signed.
Done means income, asset and employment documents are verified and the appraisal is ordered.
Done means underwriting conditions are all satisfied.
Done means the Closing Disclosure is delivered 3 business days ahead, docs signed and the loan funds.
waiting: Underwriting conditions: letters of explanation, updated bank statements, source of large deposits.
ask: Lock the rate now or float?
Buy down the rate with points
Locking protects against increases before closing.
checkin: - Done: application, appraisal ordered
- Next: underwriting review
- Needs from you: explanation for the $6,000 deposit on Sept 3
talk: Underwriting needs a letter explaining the $6,000 deposit on Sept 3 and where it came from.
That was my dad, a gift for the down payment.
Then we need a signed gift letter and his bank statement showing it. Template is in your portal.
anxieties: Will we close on time?
Did my rate lock expire?
Why do they keep asking for more documents?
notes: Standard steps; underwriting conditions vary per borrower. Regulated: TILA-RESPA (TRID) disclosure timing, GLBA privacy and FTC Safeguards, ECOA, NMLS licensing. Portal must not quote rates or give approval decisions automatically. Lenders and underwriters own the timeline.

label: Business consulting
summary: Eight-week engagement to fix scheduling bottlenecks and reset service pricing.
billing: Fixed fee per phase under a statement of work, typically 50 percent upfront and the rest on deliverables; some use monthly retainers or hourly. Source: common SOW practice (vendor and consultant guides).
ms: Done means stakeholder interviews and data review are complete and the findings memo is delivered.
Done means the recommendations are presented and the owner picks priorities.
Done means a 90-day plan with owners and dates is approved.
Done means the 30-day check-in is held and results are measured against the baseline.
waiting: The data request: job history, pricing, payroll and scheduling exports.
ask: Pilot on one service line first.
answered: Which crew pilots the new schedule?
checkin: - Done: interviews and data review
- Next: options workshop
- Needs from you: last 12 months of job export from ServiceTitan
talk: Greg, we still need the 12-month job export to finish the pricing analysis.
My office manager is on it, Friday ok?
Friday works. We'll move the workshop to next Wednesday.
anxieties: What am I getting for the fee?
When will I see results?
Is my staff data confidential?
notes: Highly bespoke; scope creep is the main risk, so change requests need approval. NDA-level confidentiality, no specific regulation. No third-party deadlines usually.

label: Recruiting / staffing search
summary: Retained search for a VP of Operations, target start in Q1.
billing: Retained fee of about 25 to 35 percent of first-year cash compensation, paid in thirds (engagement, shortlist or 30 days, placement); contingency firms bill only on hire. Sources: pin.com commission structures, Darden retained search guide.
ms: Done means the position specification is approved and the first retainer third is paid.
Done means a shortlist of 4 to 6 qualified, interested candidates is presented.
Done means finalists are interviewed and references checked.
Done means the candidate accepts the offer and a start date is set.
waiting: Interview feedback on presented candidates, quickly.
checkin: - Done: slate of 5 presented
- Next: first-round interviews
- Needs from you: feedback on candidates 2 and 4 by Tuesday
talk: Rachel, candidate 4 has another final round next week. Can you share feedback by Tuesday?
We liked her. Can she meet the CEO Monday?
I'll check and confirm today.
anxieties: How many candidates are in the pipeline?
Why is this taking so long?
What if the hire leaves early (guarantee)?
notes: Every search differs but phases are standard. Candidate personal data is private (GDPR/CCPA, EEO); share candidate reports only with authorized client users. Replacement guarantee terms. Candidate decisions are third-party timing.

label: Insurance broker (commercial)
summary: Remarket general liability, property, auto and workers comp ahead of the January 1 renewal.
billing: Commission paid by the carrier as a percentage of premium; some brokers add disclosed broker or service fees. Not billed per stage. Source: commercial renewal checklists (Massachusetts agents procedures manual, Manifestly).
ms: Done means exposures are updated and current loss runs are in hand, about 90 days before expiration.
Done means signed ACORD applications and supplementals are sent to selected carriers.
Done means firm quotes are compared in a proposal and reviewed with the client.
Done means coverage is bound before expiration, certificates issued and policies delivered.
waiting: Signed applications and updated payroll, revenue and vehicle schedules.
ask: New carrier excludes one subcontractor class.
checkin: - Done: loss runs, updated payroll
- Next: submissions to four markets
- Needs from you: signed ACORD applications
talk: Paul, applications are ready to sign. We need them back this week to get quotes before Thanksgiving.
Signed. Can you include the new excavator?
Added at $185k. Updated schedule is in your folder.
anxieties: Will my premium go up?
Am I covered for this job/contract?
When will I get my certificate?
notes: Same cycle every year, variable by line. State licensing, producer compensation disclosure rules in some states, privacy of claims data, OFAC screening. Carriers own quote and binding timing; policy expiration is a hard deadline. Portal must not imply coverage is bound until binder exists.

label: Grant writing
summary: Research, write and submit a $75,000 program grant to a community foundation.
billing: Flat fee per proposal or hourly, never a percentage of the award (Grant Professionals Association code treats commission/contingency pay as unethical). Commonly deposit at start, balance on submission. Sources: GPA, nonprofitmarketingguide.com, beancount.io grant writer guide.
ms: Done means the funder is confirmed as a fit and the deadline and requirements are mapped.
Done means the program description, outcomes and budget inputs are received.
Done means the narrative and budget are drafted and the client approved them.
Done means the application is submitted in the funder portal and confirmation is received.
waiting: Program data, budget figures and attachments such as the 990 and board list.
checkin: - Done: funder fit, intake interview
- Next: narrative draft
- Needs from you: last year's participant numbers, signed letter of support
talk: Diane, I need last year's participant numbers and outcome survey results for the need statement.
We have numbers but the survey was small. Is that okay?
Yes, we'll use it with the attendance data.
anxieties: Will we get funded?
Are we going to make the deadline?
What reporting do we owe if we win?
notes: Moderately standard. Ethics: no contingency fees, writer does not guarantee awards. Federal grants require SAM.gov/UEI registration. Funder and government own deadlines and decisions.

label: Personal injury law
summary: Auto accident claim from treatment through demand and settlement.
billing: Contingency fee, commonly about one-third of recovery (higher if litigated), plus case costs, paid only from settlement through the trust account. No per-stage billing. Source: general practice; contingency fee agreements must be in writing (ABA Model Rule 1.5(c)).
ms: Done means the fee agreement is signed and insurers are notified.
Done means the client finishes medical treatment or reaches maximum medical improvement.
Done means medical records and bills are collected and the demand package is sent.
Done means the settlement is accepted, liens resolved and funds disbursed.
waiting: Treatment updates and records of missed work and out-of-pocket costs.
ask: Offer covers bills but little for pain and suffering.
checkin: - Done: records requested
- Next: demand letter
- Needs from you: pay stubs for missed work
talk: Marcus, your last physical therapy visit is done. We're requesting records and will send the demand in about 3 weeks.
How much do you think it's worth?
We'll review the numbers together before sending.
anxieties: What is my case worth?
Why is it taking so long?
How much will I actually get after fees and liens?
notes: Classic "where's my case" practice. Privilege, HIPAA-adjacent medical records, trust accounting for settlement funds, written closing statement required for contingency cases. Insurers, courts and medical providers own timing.
